title: GitHub URL swaps — gitdiagram, gitingest, deepwiki and gitmcp for any repo
summary: Swap github.com in a repo URL for gitdiagram.com to get an architecture diagram, gitingest.com for an LLM-readable dump, deepwiki.com for generated docs, or gitmcp.io to let your agent query the repo live over MCP. Pressing the period key on a GitHub repo opens it in browser VS Code.
takeaways: gitingest.com turns a repo into one prompt-ready text file
gitmcp.io gives agents live MCP access to any public repo
deepwiki.com generates docs for undocumented projects
Press . on GitHub for instant web VS Code

title: Crypto wash trading — Ben McKenzie doc on fake volume and pump schemes
summary: Clip from the documentary 'Everyone Is Lying to You for Money' where an insider explains wash trading: one actor trading between two accounts to walk prices up, luring outsiders before dumping. The interviewee claims 90-95% of crypto volume is fake and fewer than 20 people control the market.
takeaways: Rising price on high volume can be one actor trading with themselves
Discount reported crypto volume heavily
The 90-95% fake figure is an interviewee claim, not audited data

title: Wind-chime doors — interactive web art where each country is a sounding door
summary: A personal creative-coding piece by a nomadic UI/UX designer: each country she lives in becomes a door styled on its architecture and wisdom, hung with its own wind chime sound. Inspiration only, no tutorial or live link yet.
takeaways: Personal rituals make strong concepts for interactive web art
Pair architectural visuals with ambient sound per scene

title: Conway's law — Casey Muratori on the one unbreakable rule, now for agents
summary: Casey Muratori argues Conway's law is software's only real law: once you split work among workers (people or agents) whose communication is slower than their internal compute, design iteration across that boundary is locked in as slower. 'Products look like the org chart' is a consequence, not the law itself.
takeaways: Your agent decomposition will shape the architecture you get
Put boundaries where you expect the least design iteration
Cross-boundary changes will always be slower than internal ones

title: Clipper outreach agent — Roy Lee's pay-per-view clipping army, automated
summary: Reverse-engineers Cluely founder Roy Lee's growth tactic of getting 700+ clipping accounts to post him on pay-per-view terms. An agent finds accounts your audience follows, scrapes suggested clipping accounts, pulls emails from bios, and drafts pitches pointing to raw footage and top-performing examples.
takeaways: Clippers paid per view can scale distribution cheaply
Mine suggested-account graphs to find clippers in your niche
Provide raw footage plus proven examples

title: Codex + Blender — agent-built 3D hero asset embedded with Three.js
summary: Codex generated hero-section concepts with image generation, then recreated the chosen one as a Blender model via a GitHub repo of Blender skills, fully hands-off. It imported the asset into the site with Three.js as an interactive, mouse-following, explode-and-reassemble element, and tuned it for mobile. Works in Claude Code too.
takeaways: Generate concept images first, then have the agent model the winner in Blender
Blender skills let the agent model without you knowing Blender
Check mobile performance of WebGL hero assets

title: Claude design stack — Emil Kowalski, Impeccable, taste skills plus Figma MCP
summary: Setup for professional-looking Claude-built sites: install the Emil Kowalski design and Impeccable skills for typography, spacing, layout and motion rules, add a taste skill that references great sites, then connect Figma MCP and Playwright so Claude can design, build, screenshot and test its own output.
takeaways: Design-rule skills fix the generic AI look
Give Claude Playwright so it can screenshot and check its work
Figma MCP links design and build in one loop

title: GENIUS Act stablecoins — how banks keep the T-bill yield on your cash
summary: Under the GENIUS Act banks can issue stablecoins, park the backing cash in short-term Treasury bills, keep the roughly 4% yield (the law bars passing it to holders), and repo the T-bills for liquidity. Holders can swap into tokenized Treasuries like USYC, which Binance accepts as collateral. Ends with a paid-group pitch.
takeaways: Stablecoin issuers earn the T-bill yield, holders do not
Tokenized Treasuries are how holders can capture yield
Repo gives issuers fast liquidity for redemptions

title: AI influencer pipeline — Claude-built persona monetized via Fanvue
summary: Recipe for an AI persona business: a Claude connector interviews you and designs a viral character with five consistent reference images, a Fanvue custom connector sells private content and automates DMs, and Seedance 2.5 generates Instagram videos. Thin, monetization-bait content.
takeaways: Generate a fixed reference set for character consistency
Ethically and legally murky, treat as trend reference

title: Anthropic job index audit — map your tasks to automation vs augmentation
summary: Download Anthropic's job index, combine it with the US Labor Department's O*NET task database for your role, and have an AI split your tasks by Anthropic's automation-versus-augmentation ratio. A second prompt builds a 90-day plan to automate the automatable parts and get excellent at the rest.
takeaways: Analyze your job at task level, not title level
Automate what is clearly automatable now
Invest in taste and creativity tasks AI does poorly

title: Faceless GTA 6 Shorts channel — Gemini + Claude + Higgsfield MCP clipping
summary: Sponsored Higgsfield recipe: add the Higgsfield MCP as a Claude connector, use Gemini to watch viral GTA 6 YouTube footage, then have Claude find the action peaks and crop them into vertical shorts. Income claims are speculative.
takeaways: Gemini can watch YouTube links directly
Claude plus a video MCP can auto-cut vertical clips
Paid partnership, discount the income claims

title: AI monk-style avatar ads — turning a viral trend into a product skit
summary: Method behind the viral AI monk marketing: find a trending person or format, generate a stylized Pixar-like character instead of a deceptive likeness, write an ironic script that features your product, record your own dialogue, then generate shots from a beat list and edit. The creator admits it took heavy refinement.
takeaways: Ride an already-viral format rather than inventing one
Stylize characters so you are not deceiving viewers
Record dialogue yourself for better results

title: Expired-domain rebuild — a black-hat SEO backlink tactic
summary: Buy a relevant expired domain, rebuild it from the Wayback Machine, force-index with IndexChex, prop it up with cheap niche edits, then add one contextual link to your site once it ranks and push paid traffic through it. Requires footprint hiding (separate emails, hosting, IPs). Explicitly black-hat with penalty risk.
takeaways: Inherited domain authority is the lever
Google links related domains via registration and hosting footprints
Black-hat, so risk of manual penalties

title: Katana crawler — fast JS endpoint and API route discovery for web recon
summary: ProjectDiscovery's Katana crawls web apps to surface endpoints, URLs, parameters and JavaScript files, prioritizing JS endpoints and API routes. Demoed on Kali Linux against a lab VM. Use only on systems you are authorized to test.
takeaways: Katana pulls API routes out of JavaScript early in recon
Good fit for CTFs and authorized pentests
Run against owned or permitted targets only

title: Workflow hijacking — Noma research on AI automations with no authorization
summary: Noma Labs research shows AI workflows (email auto-responders, GitHub Actions, Google email flows) leak data when an attacker simply asks, because nothing checks whether the requester is authorized. Not prompt injection, the model is doing what it's told. The fix is bringing identity and authorization into agent workflows.
takeaways: Check requester identity before an AI workflow returns data
Distinguish this from direct and indirect prompt injection
Audit email and CI automations that act on inbound messages

title: Higgsfield plugin for ChatGPT — floor plans to 3D walkthroughs with GPT-6 Astra
summary: Sponsored Higgsfield post claiming GPT-6 Astra plus the Higgsfield ChatGPT plugin turns floor plans into 3D walkthroughs, builds playable games and makes motion graphics. No transcript content survives beyond the caption.
takeaways: Paid partnership, little substance captured
Low-signal save, keep only as a trend marker

title: Subscription token arbitrage — Claude Max vs Grok Ultra API-equivalent usage
summary: Compares plan value: Claude's $200 Max is worth over $7,000/month in API usage, while Grok Ultra at $300 is claimed at over $12,000. The creator plans to switch from Claude as brain plus Codex as hands to Fable as brain plus Grokbot as hands.
takeaways: Flat subscriptions are far cheaper than API at high usage
Route planning to the smartest model and execution to the cheapest bulk tokens
Usage figures are third-party estimates

title: Data reclamation game — gamifying opt-outs from data brokers
summary: A developer built a game to make reclaiming your personal data from corporations and data brokers as engaging as signing up was, countering dark-pattern cancellation flows. Mostly framing, few specifics on which opt-outs it covers.
takeaways: Dark patterns make leaving harder than joining
Gamifying opt-outs can beat avoidance paralysis

Paid partnership, treat demos as best-case

title: Fable orchestrates, Opus executes — cutting frontier-model token spend
summary: Brain-dump your task list to Fable, have it write specs and spawn cheaper Opus subagents (in parallel worktrees) to execute, then Fable reviews and sends fixes back in a loop until it's good enough. You get top-model judgment without burning usage limits on implementation.
takeaways: Use the expensive model for planning and review only
Delegate implementation to cheaper subagents with written specs
Loop review and fix until the orchestrator approves

title: Shared second-brain MCP — team access to ICM context folders across AIs
summary: A team built an MCP server for their context-sharing platform so any AI can list and read shared ICM templates (folder-based LLM wikis with instructions and scripts) without logging in or syncing via GitHub, SharePoint or zip files. New uploads from teammates show up immediately.
takeaways: Serve shared agent context over MCP instead of file syncing
Works across different AI clients on a team

Useful for investigations, respect privacy limits
